1.explanation: The syntax definitions for Handlebars and HTMLBars live in these two files. They contain the regular-expression patterns and modes that tell highlight.js how to parse the `{{#if}}`/`{{else}}`/`{{/if}}` constructs. Because the current grammar doesn’t properly handle the `else if` sequence as two separate tokens (the keyword `else` plus a sub-expression), those modes need to be updated here. No other part of the repository handles Handlebars block syntax, so these are the two files you’ll need to fix.
1.bug_scenario: When you use a Handlebars/Glimmer template block with nested `if/else if` constructs (for example `{{#if this.userData.isLoaded}}…{{else if this.userData.isError}}…{{/if}}`), highlight.js doesn’t correctly recognize and style the `else` and the following condition. In the screenshot you can see that the keywords and the expressions are being lumped together and colored inconsistently instead of giving the `else` a distinct style and tokenizing the condition after it.

2.explanation: Both Handlebars and HTMLBars language definition files in src/languages define the mustache/block helper grammars and keyword lists (e.g. #if, /if, else). Since “else if” isn’t currently listed or parsed as a distinct keyword sequence, highlight.js falls back to treating it like ordinary text. Updating these two files to include “else” (and a combined “else if”) in the keyword modes and adjust the block-helper regular expressions will fix the broken highlighting for nested conditional blocks.
2.bug_scenario: In Handlebars (and HTMLBars) templates, block statements using “#if” and “else if” aren’t being distinguished properly by highlight.js. In the example image, “#if” is highlighted as a keyword but the “else if” line is entirely colored as plain text, so nested conditions or fallback paths don’t get the correct syntax coloring. The user expects both “if” and “else if” (and their surrounding braces) to be recognized and highlighted consistently.
